column3: “It will continue evening” is rendered “the night continues”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. “I will be surfeited restlessness” is rendered “I am continually tossing.”
“Hardened” is rendered “hardens”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Will carry in my complaint” is rendered “will ease my complaint.”
“I reject” is rendered “I waste away”; the Hebrew verb usually means “refuse,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“Set your heart to him” is rendered “are concerned about him.”
“How long will you not look away” is rendered “Will You never turn Your gaze away.”
The Hebrew reads “a burden on myself”; ancient tradition notes an older reading “on you,” and NASB follows the Hebrew.
